It's worth noting that you asked about **Catherine McCoy**, but the most prominent person by a very similar name is **Katherine McCoy** — a highly influential American graphic designer and educator. Here is an overview:

---

### Katherine McCoy — American Graphic Designer & Educator

Katherine McCoy (born October 12, 1945) is an American graphic designer and educator, best known for her work as the co-chair of the graduate Design program for Cranbrook Academy of Art.

#### Early Life & Education
McCoy was born Katherine Jane Braden in Decatur, Illinois in 1945. As a student, she first studied interior design at Michigan State University but switched to industrial design, in which field she graduated in 1967.

#### Early Career
Shortly after graduation, McCoy joined Unimark International, a design firm led by many key figures in American Modernist graphic design, including Massimo Vignelli, Ralph Eckerstrom, Jay Doblin, and Herbert Bayer. It was at the interdisciplinary Unimark offices where McCoy was exposed to the strict Swiss typographic and design approaches which came to permeate much of American corporate communications through the late 1960s and 70s.

Following Unimark, McCoy worked for a year in the corporate identity offices of the Chrysler Corporation, then joined the Boston design firm Omnigraphics, where she worked on several projects for the MIT Press with Muriel Cooper.

#### Cranbrook Academy of Art
In 1971, she founded the practice McCoy & McCoy, Inc. with her husband, Michael McCoy, and began her career in design education when she was appointed co-chair of the Cranbrook Academy of Art graduate design program.

By the 1980s, their sometimes controversial programme had established itself as one of the most innovative in American design education, producing a stream of graduates who have gone on to make their own mark in the profession.

Katherine and Michael McCoy revised the design program at Cranbrook Academy of Art: instead of deadlines and conventional exams, they offered experimentation, self-evaluation, and weekly critiques.

#### Later Teaching & Work
In 1995, McCoy left Cranbrook and joined other distinguished art institutes such as the Royal College of Art in London and Illinois Institute of Technology's Institute of Design.

Since 1997, she and Michael have hosted the High Ground Design Conversation, an annual gathering of design curators, critics, and educators.

#### Awards & Honors
In 1983, she was elected to a 2-year term as the president of the IDSA (Industrial Designers Society of America), not only the first woman but the youngest person to do so.

In 1994, the McCoys were jointly awarded a Chrysler Award for Innovation in Design.

Since its founding, McCoy & McCoy has won more than 150 design awards.
